Good morning, my name's Angela Gardner, General Manager, utilities and environment.
This first approval report recommends extending the current pause on carbon charge collection for sastion light and power until December 31, 2026.
This pause was initially implemented in April of 2025,
following the government of Saskatchewan's decision to suspend the industrial carbon charge under its output based performance standards program.
Extending the pause ensures fairness for light and power,
customers by aligning rates with sast power and maintaining the temporary reduction in electricity costs introduced earlier this year.
Without this extension, sastion light and power would be paying higher rates despite the elimination of associated costs,
creating inequity compared to sast power customers.
Financially, continuing the pause will maintain the reduction in residential electricity rates by an average of 6.79 percent,
saving a typical household about $10.46 per month.
While sastion light and power is revenue would decline by 15.12 million.
In 2026, this would be offset by lower bulk power costs and reduced grant and new payments resulting in a net surplus per sastion light and power.
However, the city overall may experience a negative corporate impact of approximately $476,000 if the pause continues for the entire year.
If a deficit is experienced as the result of the pause, the administration will bring forward option so that the mill rate is not impacted.
The administration will continue to monitor provincial and federal policy changes and report back to city council by December 2026 or sooner if required.

The Organics Processing Facility Project is progressing as a city on solution to managing the process.
We're going to be managing the processing of curbside and depo organics following challenges with the previous contractor.
The facility will process up to 40,000 tons annually and incorporate advanced auto control electric powered equipment and environmental safeguards.
Three pilot programs informed the design and operations of the new facility and communication addressed concerns such as order management and winter operations.
Provincial permitting activities are underway and the facility is expected to open in 2027.
Once operational the Organics Processing Facility will replace the West Compost Depot and support expanded organics diversion programs including multi unit and curbside initiatives.
Earlier this year the federal government provided $8.4 million from the Canadian Housing Infrastructure Fund to this project.

The federal funding program required additional specifications and scope related to greenhouse gas mitigation measures like electric equipment and low carbon concrete resulting in additional costs of just under $1 million which is over and above the approved scope and budget.
In addition construction of the facility was recently tendered and all bids came in over the approved budget.

Work is currently underway to develop a revised tendering process to reduce the contract, durs, risks and address other feedback received from the initial procurement with an intent to reduce the costs.

To accommodate the new requirements and the feedback from recent procurement the administration recommends increasing the project budget from $22.1 million to $30.5 million funded entirely by the $8.4 million from the federal government.
Upon completion of the project if the full budget is not required the city's borrowing could be reduced based on the actual funds required to complete this as per regular processes.

Despite higher capital costs the construction of the Organics Processing Facility remains the most cost effective option offering long-term price stability and approximately $1 million in annual operating savings compared to outsourcing to a third party.

In addition to the recommendations regarding the budget the administration is recommending that the receiving haul be exempt from the high performance civic building policy requirements due to its industrial nature.
Those sustainability features such as heat recovery remained part of the design.

The diversity equity and inclusion advisory committee continued its mandate in 2025 advising on issues related to diversity equity and inclusion across Saskatoon.
The committee focused on key areas such as anti racism anti oppression and accessibility while maintaining strong representation from community organizations and public members.

Major accomplishments as outlined in their annual report include reviewing and updating the cultural diversity and race relations policy managing the education and awareness fund and planning initiatives to strengthen committee engagement.

The committee also collaborated with the reconciliation equity diversity and inclusion office to update the living and harmony awards categories and format ensuring alignment with the evolving community needs.

Throughout the year, the diversity equity inclusion advisory committee approved sponsorships for cultural and educational events supported public outreach efforts and developed community continuity documents to guide future leadership transitions.
Reports and recommendations were submitted to city council and standing policy committees including a letter of support for the multi year accessibility plan.
In total, the committee allocated $15,100 to support diverse community initiatives such as cultural festivals, refugee awareness events and intercultural dialogues.
Suggested areas for future consideration in their work plans include enhancing public presence through the city's communication channels and creating values focused opening statements for meetings.
